title: Algebraic closure in a finitely generated field extension is finite
statement: Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $k_{\mathrm{alg}}\subseteq K$ be the algebraic closure of $k$ in $K$, namely the subfield of elements of $K$ algebraic over $k$ [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure]. Then $k_{\mathrm{alg}}/k$ is finite: $[k_{\mathrm{alg}}:k]<\infty$.

proof.text: Choose finite field generators $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ of $K/k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis], choose $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in K$ algebraically independent over $k$ such that $K$ is algebraic over $L=k(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. Thus the $a_j$ are algebraic over $L$, and $L(a_1,\ldots,a_s)=K$ because $k\subseteq L\subseteq K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] over $L$ to obtain $n=[K:L]<\infty$.

source.place: Tag 037J proof, first paragraph; finite generation made explicit using Tags 030F and 09GH

proof.text: Fix any finite intermediate extension $k\subseteq k'\subseteq K$, and put $m=[k':k]$. Every $b\in k'$ is algebraic over $k$: the $m+1$ powers $1,b,\ldots,b^m$ are linearly dependent over $k$, giving a nonzero polynomial vanishing at $b$. Hence [lem-zl-independence-algebraic-base] makes the tuple $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ algebraically independent over $k'$ as well. For $0\le j\le r$, set $F_j=k(x_1,\ldots,x_j)$ and $E_j=k'(x_1,\ldots,x_j)$. Inductively $E_j/F_j$ is finite of degree $m$: for $j=0$ this is $k'/k$. At the successor, independence says that $x_{j+1}$ is transcendental over $E_j$ (and therefore over $F_j$): if a nonzero polynomial over $E_j$ vanished at $x_{j+1}$, express its finitely many coefficients as quotients of polynomials in $x_1,\ldots,x_j$ over $k′$ and multiply by the product of the nonzero denominators. At least one coefficient stays nonzero, so the resulting nonzero polynomial in $j+1$ variables over $k′$ contradicts independence. Evaluation $P(T)/Q(T)\mapsto P(x_{j+1})/Q(x_{j+1})$ identifies the rational function fields over $E_j,F_j$ with $E_{j+1},F_{j+1}$, respectively; denominators stay nonzero by transcendence, and every element of the generated field is such a fraction [def-weil-rational-function-field]. The two evaluation maps commute with coefficient inclusion, so [lem-zl-rational-function-degree] gives $[E_{j+1}:F_{j+1}]=[E_j:F_j]=m$. Consequently $[k'(x_1,\ldots,x_r):L]=[k':k]$.

source.place: Tag 037J proof, application of Tag 0G1M; the finite-variable equality is obtained by elementary induction from its one-variable case

proof.text: The inclusion $k'(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\subseteq K$ is an inclusion of $L$-vector spaces, so any $L$-linearly independent family in the smaller field remains independent in $K$. Its dimension over $L$ is therefore at most $n$. By step 2, $[k':k]\le n$ for every finite intermediate field $k'$ of $K/k$.

source.place: Tag 037J proof, displayed inequality comparing intermediate degrees with [K:L]

proof.text: By [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure], $A=k_{\mathrm{alg}}$ is a subfield of $K$ containing $k$ and every element of $A$ is algebraic over $k$. Its finite intermediate fields have degrees in the nonempty finite set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ (the field $k$ has degree one). Choose one, $k'$, of maximal degree $m$. A $k$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ of $k'$ also generates $k'$ as a field: the generated field contains their entire $k$-linear span. For any $\alpha\in A$, [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] applied to $b_1,\ldots,b_m,\alpha$ shows that $k'(\alpha)/k$ is finite. It is contained in $A$, so maximality gives $[k'(\alpha):k]\le m$. The inclusion $k'\subseteq k'(\alpha)$ gives the reverse dimension inequality. Equality of these finite dimensions forces equality of the two vector subspaces, so $\alpha\in k'$. Therefore $A=k'$ and $[A:k]=m<\infty$.

source.place: Tag 037J proof, final sentence: explicit maximal-degree argument for the bounded degrees of finite subextensions
